stem: A client with pulmonary arterial hypertension receives a continuous IV epoprostenol infusion through a central line. The pump alarms and stops, and the client becomes dyspneic with an SpO2 of 86% and blood pressure 94/60. Which action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Restart the infusion immediately with the backup pump and supply oxygen
options.B: Wait for the pharmacy to deliver a new cassette before restarting
options.C: Flush the central line with 10 mL of saline to clear a clot
options.D: Give a fluid bolus and recheck the oxygen saturation and pressure in 30 minutes

correct: A) Restart the infusion immediately with the backup pump and supply oxygen
rationale: Sudden interruption can cause rebound pulmonary hypertension and collapse, so the infusion is restored right away.
B: waiting for a new cassette leaves the client without drug.
C: a forceful flush does not address the pump failure and can dislodge a clot.
D: a fluid bolus can worsen right heart strain and a delay is unsafe.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Respiratory (Pulmonary hypertension) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A client has right lower lobe pneumonia and an SpO2 of 86% on 4 L/min nasal cannula while supine. Which position should the nurse use to improve oxygenation?

options.A: Trendelenburg to promote drainage of the bronchial secretions
options.B: Supine with the head of the bed flat
options.C: Left side-lying with the unaffected lung dependent
options.D: Right side-lying with the pneumonia dependent

correct: C) Left side-lying with the unaffected lung dependent
rationale: The better-ventilated lung gets more blood flow when dependent, which improves ventilation-perfusion matching.
A: a head-down position raises abdominal pressure on the diaphragm.
B: a flat position reduces lung volumes and worsens oxygenation.
D: the diseased lung receives more blood flow and less ventilation, worsening the mismatch.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Respiratory (Positioning) · Hard · Application · Safety

stem: A client started lisinopril 6 weeks ago and has a persistent dry, tickling cough. The chest x-ray and lung examination are normal, and there is no fever. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Oral antibiotics for presumed bronchitis
options.B: A cough suppressant added to the lisinopril
options.C: An increase in the lisinopril dose to control the inflammation
options.D: A change to an angiotensin receptor blocker

correct: D) A change to an angiotensin receptor blocker
rationale: ACE inhibitors commonly cause a dry cough, and switching to an angiotensin receptor blocker resolves it.
A: no infection is present, so antibiotics do not help.
B: masking the cough continues the underlying cause.
C: a higher dose worsens the cough.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Pharmacology in Medical-Surgical Care (ACE inhibitors) · Hard · Application · Adverse Effect

stem: A client receiving IV phenytoin develops swelling, purple discoloration, and pain in the hand distal to the IV site 12 hours after the infusion. Pulses are present. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Elevation of the limb with supportive care and monitoring for compartment syndrome
options.B: Massage of the hand to improve circulation
options.C: Warm soaks and a repeat phenytoin infusion at the same site in the next few hours as scheduled
options.D: A tourniquet above the site to limit swelling

correct: A) Elevation of the limb with supportive care and monitoring for compartment syndrome
rationale: Phenytoin is a tissue irritant that can cause delayed soft-tissue injury, so elevation and monitoring are needed.
B: massage can damage injured tissue.
C: repeating the infusion at the injured site worsens the injury.
D: a tourniquet worsens ischemia.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Anticonvulsant adverse effects) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Complication

stem: A client with a deep foot wound 8 days ago has jaw stiffness and painful neck muscle spasms triggered by noise. The client has no fever and has never been immunized. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Give a tetanus booster and send the client home
options.B: Encourage the client to eat solid food to exercise the jaw muscles
options.C: Place the client in a quiet, dim room and prepare for airway support, tetanus immune globulin, and wound care
options.D: Apply a hot pack to the neck and give an NSAID

correct: C) Place the client in a quiet, dim room and prepare for airway support, tetanus immune globulin, and wound care
rationale: Jaw stiffness and spasms triggered by stimuli in an unimmunized client suggest tetanus, which needs minimal stimulation, airway readiness, and immune globulin.
A: a booster does not neutralize existing toxin.
B: chewing solid food with trismus risks aspiration and spasm.
D: heat and an NSAID do not treat tetanus or protect the airway.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Tetanus) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Emergency

stem: A client with a ventriculoperitoneal shunt has a severe headache, vomiting, drowsiness, and new difficulty looking upward. Which action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Keep the head of the bed elevated and arrange urgent neurosurgical evaluation for shunt malfunction
options.B: Give acetaminophen and reassess in 4 hours
options.C: Pump the shunt reservoir repeatedly to restore drainage
options.D: Lay the client flat to relieve the headache

correct: A) Keep the head of the bed elevated and arrange urgent neurosurgical evaluation for shunt malfunction
rationale: Headache, vomiting, drowsiness, and an upward gaze palsy suggest raised pressure from shunt failure, which is an emergency.
B: waiting 4 hours risks herniation.
C: repeated pumping can damage the shunt without instruction.
D: lying flat raises the intracranial pressure.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Shunt malfunction) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A client who has taken haloperidol for 4 years has new lip smacking, tongue protrusion, and writhing finger movements. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Reassurance that the movements are related to anxiety
options.B: An increase in the haloperidol dose to suppress the abnormal movements
options.C: Review of the antipsychotic and a standardized movement assessment
options.D: An anticholinergic such as benztropine to stop the movements

correct: C) Review of the antipsychotic and a standardized movement assessment
rationale: Late-onset orofacial and limb movements suggest tardive dyskinesia, which needs drug review and structured assessment.
A: the movements are neurologic, not anxiety-related.
B: more drug can mask the movements while the injury continues.
D: anticholinergics can worsen tardive dyskinesia.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Movement disorders) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Adverse Effect

stem: A client who has taken omeprazole for 4 years reports muscle cramps and palpitations. Telemetry shows frequent PVCs, potassium is 3.4 mEq/L, and calcium is 7.9 mg/dL. Which laboratory test should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Cardiac troponin with each shift
options.B: Serum amylase level with a lipase
options.C: Thyroid-stimulating hormone with free thyroxine
options.D: Serum magnesium level with replacement if low

correct: D) Serum magnesium level with replacement if low
rationale: Long-term proton pump inhibitors can cause hypomagnesemia, which also causes hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, and ectopy.
A: ectopy here has an electrolyte cause.
B: pancreatic enzymes do not explain these findings.
C: thyroid disease does not explain the combined electrolyte pattern.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Gastrointestinal (Acid suppression adverse effects) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Adverse Effect

stem: A client 5 days after a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt becomes confused with a flapping tremor and sleep-wake reversal. Ammonia is elevated. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Lactulose or rifaximin with a search for precipitating factors
options.B: A benzodiazepine to treat the agitation and the sleep-wake problem
options.C: Removal of the shunt before any other treatment
options.D: Protein supplements to improve nutrition and reduce confusion

correct: A) Lactulose or rifaximin with a search for precipitating factors
rationale: A portosystemic shunt can precipitate encephalopathy, which is treated with ammonia-lowering therapy and a search for triggers.
B: benzodiazepines worsen encephalopathy.
C: shunt reduction is reserved for refractory cases.
D: large protein loads can raise ammonia.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Gastrointestinal (Hepatic encephalopathy) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Complication

stem: A client 2 months after gastric surgery has sweating, tremor, and a glucose of 52 mg/dL about 2 hours after meals. Which instruction should the nurse give?

options.A: Lie flat and drink juice during the meal to slow the gastric emptying and absorption
options.B: Eat small frequent meals higher in protein and fat with fewer simple sugars
options.C: Eat a large high-carbohydrate meal and drink fluids with it
options.D: Skip meals and take a sugary drink between them

correct: B) Eat small frequent meals higher in protein and fat with fewer simple sugars
rationale: Late dumping causes reactive hypoglycemia from rapid carbohydrate absorption, so simple sugars are limited and protein and fat are emphasized.
A: juice with the meal adds simple sugar and worsens the swing.
C: large carbohydrate meals and fluids worsen the swings.
D: skipping meals with sugary drinks worsens the swings.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Gastrointestinal (Postgastrectomy nutrition) · Hard · Application · Teaching

stem: A client 6 hours after ERCP reports severe epigastric pain radiating to the back with nausea. Lipase is 5 times the upper normal limit. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: NPO status with IV fluids and analgesia for post-procedure pancreatitis
options.B: Discharge instructions as pain after ERCP is expected and should settle soon
options.C: An NSAID and restricted fluids to protect the kidneys
options.D: A regular diet and an antacid for gas pain

correct: A) NPO status with IV fluids and analgesia for post-procedure pancreatitis
rationale: Pain with markedly raised lipase after ERCP indicates pancreatitis, which needs fluids, analgesia, and bowel rest.
B: discharge risks complications.
C: restricting fluids worsens pancreatic injury.
D: feeding a regular diet worsens pancreatitis.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Gastrointestinal (Procedure complication) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Complication

stem: A 22-year-old man has sudden severe left scrotal pain with nausea that began 2 hours ago. The scrotum is swollen, the left testis is high-riding, and the cremasteric reflex is absent. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Oral antibiotics and scrotal elevation for epididymitis
options.B: A routine ultrasound next week with ice packs and an NSAID for comfort
options.C: Emergency surgical exploration without waiting for imaging results
options.D: Reassurance and an NSAID for a presumed muscle strain

correct: C) Emergency surgical exploration without waiting for imaging results
rationale: These findings suggest testicular torsion, where salvage depends on surgery within hours.
A: antibiotics do not relieve torsion.
B: a delay of a week risks loss of the testis.
D: an NSAID and reassurance delay an emergency.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Renal and Urinary (Genitourinary emergency) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A client with diabetes taking empagliflozin has severe perineal pain, swelling, and dusky skin with crepitus. Temperature is 39.4°C and blood pressure is 86/50. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Emergency surgical debridement with broad-spectrum antibiotics and stopping the SGLT2 inhibitor
options.B: Warm sitz baths and an outpatient surgical visit
options.C: Oral antibiotics and a topical antifungal for a yeast infection
options.D: An increased empagliflozin dose to improve glucose control

correct: A) Emergency surgical debridement with broad-spectrum antibiotics and stopping the SGLT2 inhibitor
rationale: Pain, swelling, crepitus, and shock in the perineum suggest necrotizing infection, a rare complication of SGLT2 inhibitors.
B: an outpatient visit delays life-saving surgery.
C: oral therapy does not treat necrotizing infection.
D: continuing or increasing the drug adds risk.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Renal and Urinary (Necrotizing infection) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A client with a known pituitary adenoma has a sudden severe headache, visual field loss, double vision, blood pressure 78/44, and sodium 124 mEq/L. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: A triptan for the severe headache
options.B: IV hydrocortisone and urgent neurosurgical evaluation for pituitary hemorrhage
options.C: Oral analgesics and an outpatient MRI next week
options.D: Fluid restriction and a vasopressin infusion

correct: B) IV hydrocortisone and urgent neurosurgical evaluation for pituitary hemorrhage
rationale: Sudden headache with visual loss and hypotension in a client with an adenoma suggests pituitary apoplexy with adrenal insufficiency.
A: a triptan does not treat hemorrhage and may cause vasoconstriction.
C: outpatient care delays emergency treatment.
D: restriction and vasopressin worsen the hypotension and hyponatremia.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Endocrine (Pituitary emergency) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Emergency

stem: A client taking dabigatran has brisk gastrointestinal bleeding with hypotension and a creatinine of 2.4 mg/dL. Which medication should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Vitamin K IV
options.B: Fresh frozen plasma as the specific reversal agent
options.C: Idarucizumab to reverse the anticoagulant effect
options.D: Protamine sulfate

correct: C) Idarucizumab to reverse the anticoagulant effect
rationale: Idarucizumab is the specific reversal agent for dabigatran.
A: vitamin K reverses warfarin.
B: plasma does not specifically reverse dabigatran.
D: protamine reverses heparin.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Hematology (Anticoagulant reversal) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Antidote

stem: A client has a platelet count of 8,000/mm3, gum bleeding, and scattered petechiae with no other abnormal findings. Which prescription should the nurse question?

options.A: Intravenous immune globulin
options.B: Platelet transfusion if life-threatening bleeding occurs
options.C: Prednisone 1 mg/kg by mouth daily
options.D: Intramuscular ketorolac for headache

correct: D) Intramuscular ketorolac for headache
rationale: NSAIDs impair platelet function, and intramuscular injections risk hematoma at this platelet count.
A: immune globulin raises the platelet count quickly.
B: transfusion is reserved for life-threatening bleeding.
C: corticosteroids are first-line therapy.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Hematology (Immune thrombocytopenia) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Contraindication

stem: A client with Hodgkin lymphoma is scheduled for stem cell transplantation and needs red blood cells. Which product should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Washed red blood cells with acetaminophen premedication
options.B: Irradiated and leukoreduced red blood cells
options.C: Fresh whole blood with no filtration
options.D: Standard unirradiated red blood cells from a family donor

correct: B) Irradiated and leukoreduced red blood cells
rationale: Irradiation prevents transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease in clients at risk, and leukoreduction lowers other reactions.
A: washing and premedication do not prevent graft-versus-host disease.
C: unfiltered fresh whole blood is the highest risk product.
D: unirradiated cells, especially from relatives, carry a graft-versus-host risk.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Hematology (Transfusion safety) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Safety

stem: A client with chronic kidney disease (eGFR 28) has an acutely hot, swollen first metatarsophalangeal joint. Which prescription should the nurse question?

options.A: Ice and rest of the affected joint
options.B: Prednisone 30 mg by mouth daily for 5 days
options.C: Ibuprofen 800 mg by mouth three times daily
options.D: Colchicine at a reduced dose adjusted for kidney function

correct: C) Ibuprofen 800 mg by mouth three times daily
rationale: NSAIDs can worsen kidney function in advanced kidney disease and are avoided.
A: ice and rest relieve symptoms.
B: a short steroid course is an accepted option.
D: dose-adjusted colchicine is an accepted option.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Musculoskeletal (Acute gout) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Contraindication

stem: A client with rheumatoid arthritis is starting infliximab. Which preparation should the nurse ensure is completed before the first dose?

options.A: A baseline bone density scan
options.B: A fasting lipid panel
options.C: A pulmonary function test for asthma and chronic cough
options.D: Screening for latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B

correct: D) Screening for latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B
rationale: TNF inhibitors can reactivate latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B, so screening comes first.
A: bone density is not required for starting this drug.
B: lipid testing is not required for starting this drug.
C: asthma testing is not required for starting this drug.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Musculoskeletal (Biologic therapy) · Hard · Application · Safety

stem: A client receiving a nerve block with bupivacaine reports perioral numbness and ringing in the ears, then has a seizure. Blood pressure falls to 78/40 and heart rate to 48. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Stopping the injection and giving IV lipid emulsion along with airway support
options.B: Giving epinephrine IM for anaphylaxis
options.C: Observation with repeat vital signs in 30 minutes
options.D: Giving additional bupivacaine to deepen the block

correct: A) Stopping the injection and giving IV lipid emulsion along with airway support
rationale: Perioral numbness, tinnitus, seizure, and cardiovascular collapse suggest local anesthetic systemic toxicity, treated with lipid emulsion and support.
B: the picture is toxic, not allergic.
C: a 30-minute delay is unsafe.
D: more drug worsens the toxicity.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Perioperative (Regional anesthesia) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Antidote

stem: A 70-year-old man weighs 70 kg and has a serum creatinine of 1.4 mg/dL. Using the Cockcroft-Gault equation ((140 − age) × weight ÷ (72 × creatinine)), what is his estimated creatinine clearance?

options.A: About 97 mL/min
options.B: About 69 mL/min
options.C: About 49 mL/min
options.D: About 24 mL/min

correct: C) About 49 mL/min
rationale: A: this doubles the calculated value.
B: this omits the creatinine from the denominator.
D: this halves the calculated value.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Renal and Urinary (Kidney function estimate) · Hard · Application · Monitoring

stem: A client weighing 75 kg is prescribed a heparin bolus of 80 units/kg. The vial contains 5,000 units/mL. How many milliliters should the nurse draw up?

options.A: 1.2 mL
options.B: 12 mL
options.C: 0.6 mL
options.D: 1.5 mL

correct: A) 1.2 mL
rationale: The dose is 80 × 75 = 6,000 units, and 6,000 ÷ 5,000 = 1.2 mL.
B: this is a decimal error.
C: this is the volume for 40 units/kg.
D: this is the volume for 100 units/kg.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Hematology (Anticoagulant dosing) · Hard · Application · Safety

stem: A client weighing 84 kg with septic shock is prescribed 30 mL/kg of crystalloid over 3 hours. What infusion rate should the nurse set?

options.A: 420 mL/hr
options.B: 252 mL/hr
options.C: 840 mL/hr
options.D: 2,520 mL/hr

correct: C) 840 mL/hr
rationale: The volume is 30 × 84 = 2,520 mL, and 2,520 ÷ 3 = 840 mL/hr.
A: this spreads the volume over 6 hours.
B: this spreads the volume over 10 hours.
D: this is the total volume, not the hourly rate.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Infection Control (Septic shock resuscitation) · Hard · Application · Safety

stem: A client has a sodium of 130 mEq/L, glucose of 540 mg/dL, and BUN of 28 mg/dL. Using osmolality = 2 × sodium + glucose ÷ 18 + BUN ÷ 2.8, what is the calculated serum osmolality?

options.A: 330 mOsm/kg
options.B: 270 mOsm/kg
options.C: 290 mOsm/kg
options.D: 300 mOsm/kg

correct: D) 300 mOsm/kg
rationale: 2 × 130 = 260, glucose 540 ÷ 18 = 30, and BUN 28 ÷ 2.8 = 10, giving 300 mOsm/kg.
A: this adds extra glucose and BUN contributions.
B: this omits the glucose contribution.
C: this omits the BUN contribution.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Endocrine (Osmolality calculation) · Hard · Application · Assessment

stem: A client opens the eyes only to painful stimulation, says inappropriate words, and withdraws from pain. What is the Glasgow Coma Scale score?
rationale: Eyes to pain score 2, inappropriate words 3, and withdrawal from pain 4, for a total of 9.
B: this scores the verbal response as confused and the motor response as localizing.
C: this scores the eye opening to voice.
D: this scores the motor response as flexion and verbal as sounds.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Level of consciousness) · Hard · Application · Assessment

stem: A 72-year-old client with pneumonia is confused, has a BUN of 26 mg/dL, a respiratory rate of 32, and a blood pressure of 84/50. What is the CURB-65 score and what does it suggest?

options.A: 3, indicating moderate severity suitable for outpatient care
options.B: 4, indicating high severity with no need to consider intensive care or close monitoring on the ward
options.C: 5, indicating high severity that calls for admission with consideration of intensive care
options.D: 1, indicating low severity suitable for home treatment

correct: C) 5, indicating high severity that calls for admission with consideration of intensive care
rationale: Confusion, BUN above 19 mg/dL, respiratory rate of 30 or more, low blood pressure, and age 65 or older each score 1, giving 5.
A: this undercounts the criteria met.
B: the score is 5, which calls for consideration of intensive care.
D: this undercounts the criteria met.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Respiratory (Pneumonia severity) · Hard · Application · Assessment

stem: A 72-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation has hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and heart failure but no prior stroke. What is her CHA2DS2-VASc score and what does it suggest?

options.A: 1, indicating anticoagulation is optional in this client
options.B: 5, indicating oral anticoagulation is recommended
options.C: 2, indicating no therapy is needed
options.D: 3, indicating aspirin is sufficient

correct: B) 5, indicating oral anticoagulation is recommended
rationale: Heart failure, hypertension, age 65 to 74, diabetes, and female sex each add 1 point, giving 5.
A: this undercounts the risk factors.
C: this undercounts the risk factors.
D: this undercounts the risk factors.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Cardiovascular (Stroke risk in atrial fibrillation) · Hard · Application · Assessment

stem: A client was last known well at 2330 and arrives at the hospital at 0215 the next day with right-sided weakness. Using a 4.5-hour window from last known well for IV thrombolysis, how much time remains?

options.A: 1 hour 45 minutes
options.B: 2 hours 45 minutes
options.C: 45 minutes
options.D: 2 hours 15 minutes

correct: A) 1 hour 45 minutes
rationale: 2 hours 45 minutes have elapsed since 2330, leaving 4 hours 30 minutes minus 2 hours 45 minutes, or 1 hour 45 minutes.
B: this is the elapsed time, not the time remaining.
C: this undercounts the time remaining.
D: this miscalculates the elapsed time.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Stroke time window) · Hard · Application · Monitoring

stem: A client with heart failure and chronic kidney disease is prescribed a sodium phosphate bowel preparation for colonoscopy. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Give the preparation with extra oral fluids as prescribed
options.B: Question the prescription and anticipate a polyethylene glycol preparation instead
options.C: Give the preparation and hold the client's diuretic and fluid intake for the rest of the day
options.D: Give half of the preparation and the rest after the procedure

correct: B) Question the prescription and anticipate a polyethylene glycol preparation instead
rationale: Sodium phosphate preparations can cause phosphate nephropathy and fluid and electrolyte shifts, so they are avoided in kidney and heart disease.
A: extra fluids do not remove the kidney risk.
C: holding the diuretic does not remove the phosphate risk and can cause overload.
D: splitting the dose after the procedure is not a valid plan.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Gastrointestinal (Bowel preparation) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Contraindication

stem: A client with a documented prior anaphylactic reaction to iodinated contrast needs an urgent contrast-enhanced CT for suspected aortic dissection. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Cancellation of all imaging as contrast is contraindicated
options.B: Contrast given with no preparation as the study is urgent
options.C: Premedication with acetaminophen and a delay of 24 hours
options.D: Premedication with a corticosteroid and an antihistamine with the study done under close monitoring

correct: D) Premedication with a corticosteroid and an antihistamine with the study done under close monitoring
rationale: When imaging is urgent, accelerated premedication and monitored administration balance the risk against the need.
A: withholding imaging risks missing a lethal diagnosis.
B: giving contrast without preparation to a client with prior anaphylaxis is dangerous.
C: acetaminophen does not prevent the reaction and a delay is unsafe.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Contrast reaction) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Safety

stem: Which client requires further evaluation before an MRI scan?

options.A: Client with a coronary stent placed 2 years ago and no symptoms
options.B: Client with a titanium hip replacement
options.C: Client with a pacemaker implanted in 2005 with no MRI labeling
options.D: Client with amalgam dental fillings

correct: C) Client with a pacemaker implanted in 2005 with no MRI labeling
rationale: An older device without MRI labeling can heat, move, or malfunction in the magnetic field.
A: modern coronary stents are generally safe in MRI.
B: titanium implants are generally safe in MRI.
D: dental fillings are generally safe in MRI.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Perioperative (Imaging safety) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Safety

stem: A client with severe headache, fever, and neck stiffness has papilledema and a new unequal pupil. A lumbar puncture is prescribed. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Anticipate head imaging first and antibiotics without waiting for the puncture
options.B: Obtain consent and proceed with the puncture immediately
options.C: Position the client in the knee-chest position and proceed with the lumbar puncture
options.D: Give a sedative and proceed with the puncture to avoid delay

correct: A) Anticipate head imaging first and antibiotics without waiting for the puncture
rationale: Papilledema and a pupil change suggest raised pressure, and puncture risks herniation, so imaging comes first and antibiotics should not wait.
B: consent does not remove the danger.
C: proceeding risks herniation.
D: sedation hides neurologic changes and does not reduce the risk.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Procedure safety) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Contraindication

stem: Before an arterial puncture of the radial artery, the nurse performs a modified Allen test. The hand remains pale 10 seconds after the ulnar artery is released. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Repeat the test with the hand lower than the heart and then proceed
options.B: Proceed with the puncture and apply a warm compress afterward
options.C: Proceed as pallor shows the radial artery is intact
options.D: Avoid using that radial artery and select another site

correct: D) Avoid using that radial artery and select another site
rationale: A hand that stays pale shows inadequate ulnar collateral flow, so puncturing the radial artery risks ischemia.
A: changing position does not alter the collateral flow.
B: a warm compress does not prevent ischemia after the puncture.
C: pallor shows poor collateral circulation, not an intact radial artery.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Critical Care (Arterial sampling) · Hard · Application · Safety

stem: An adult has a severe sore throat, a muffled voice, drooling, a tripod position, and stridor. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Examine the throat with a tongue blade to see the epiglottis
options.B: Give oral antibiotics and send the client for outpatient imaging
options.C: Keep the client upright, minimize stimulation, and prepare for emergency airway management
options.D: Lay the client flat for a throat swab and chest x-ray

correct: C) Keep the client upright, minimize stimulation, and prepare for emergency airway management
rationale: These findings suggest epiglottitis, where manipulation or lying flat can trigger complete obstruction.
A: a tongue blade can provoke laryngospasm and obstruction.
B: outpatient care is unsafe with stridor.
D: lying flat can close the airway.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Respiratory (Airway emergency) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A client with a painful vesicular rash on the forehead has a vesicle on the tip of the nose and a red, painful eye. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Cool compresses and a recheck in 2 weeks
options.B: Urgent ophthalmology evaluation and antiviral therapy
options.C: Contact lenses to protect the cornea during healing
options.D: Topical steroid eye drops without any further evaluation

correct: B) Urgent ophthalmology evaluation and antiviral therapy
rationale: A vesicle on the nasal tip suggests nasociliary involvement and a risk of vision-threatening eye disease.
A: a 2-week delay risks permanent vision loss.
C: contact lenses can worsen corneal injury and infection.
D: steroid drops without evaluation can worsen viral keratitis.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Sensory (Herpes zoster ophthalmicus) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Emergency

stem: A client admitted for cellulitis who uses heroin daily has yawning, sweating, dilated pupils, abdominal cramps, and a heart rate of 112 about 24 hours after the last use. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Haloperidol for the restlessness with no other treatment
options.B: Naloxone to reverse the symptoms
options.C: Restriction to the room until the symptoms settle
options.D: Assessment with a withdrawal scale and treatment with buprenorphine or methadone as prescribed

correct: D) Assessment with a withdrawal scale and treatment with buprenorphine or methadone as prescribed
rationale: These findings indicate opioid withdrawal, treated with scored assessment and opioid agonist therapy.
A: haloperidol does not treat withdrawal and lowers the seizure threshold.
B: naloxone would worsen withdrawal.
C: restriction does not treat the withdrawal and increases distress.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Opioid withdrawal) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Monitoring

stem: A client who took a large amount of diphenhydramine has hot, dry, flushed skin, dilated pupils, a heart rate of 128, urinary retention, and agitation. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Supportive care with benzodiazepines for agitation and cooling measures
options.B: Beta blockers to slow the heart rate without any other supportive therapy
options.C: Naloxone to reverse the sedation
options.D: Bethanechol to relieve the urinary retention

correct: A) Supportive care with benzodiazepines for agitation and cooling measures
rationale: Anticholinergic toxicity is managed with supportive care, cooling, and benzodiazepines for agitation.
B: a beta blocker alone does not treat the toxidrome.
C: no opioid is involved.
D: a cholinergic drug can worsen toxicity in an overdose with agitation and tachycardia.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Anticholinergic toxicity) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Monitoring

stem: A client who drank antifreeze has an anion gap metabolic acidosis, an osmolar gap, and calcium oxalate crystals in the urine. Which medication should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Acetylcysteine
options.B: Fomepizole with preparation for hemodialysis
options.C: Activated charcoal as the sole treatment at this stage
options.D: Naloxone

correct: B) Fomepizole with preparation for hemodialysis
rationale: Fomepizole blocks the enzyme that converts ethylene glycol to toxic metabolites.
A: acetylcysteine treats acetaminophen toxicity.
C: charcoal does not bind alcohols well.
D: naloxone reverses opioids.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Toxic alcohol poisoning) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Antidote

stem: A client develops cyanosis and an SpO2 of 85% after benzocaine throat spray. The SpO2 does not improve with 100% oxygen, and blood drawn is chocolate-brown. Which medication should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Hydroxocobalamin IV for the suspected cyanide toxicity
options.B: Flumazenil
options.C: Naloxone
options.D: Methylene blue IV with continued oxygen

correct: D) Methylene blue IV with continued oxygen
rationale: Chocolate-brown blood with refractory hypoxemia after benzocaine indicates methemoglobinemia, treated with methylene blue.
A: hydroxocobalamin treats cyanide poisoning.
B: flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines.
C: naloxone reverses opioids.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Methemoglobinemia) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Antidote

stem: A client with blunt trauma has an unstable pelvis, blood at the urethral meatus, and a blood pressure of 82/50. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Log-roll the client repeatedly to inspect the back
options.B: Apply a pelvic binder, avoid inserting a urinary catheter, and prepare for blood products
options.C: Insert an indwelling catheter to monitor hourly output
options.D: Rock the pelvis to check stability and then insert a catheter

correct: B) Apply a pelvic binder, avoid inserting a urinary catheter, and prepare for blood products
rationale: A pelvic binder reduces bleeding, and blood at the meatus suggests urethral injury, so a catheter is not inserted blindly.
A: repeated rolling disturbs the clot and the pelvis.
C: blind catheterization can convert a partial urethral injury to a complete one.
D: rocking the pelvis can dislodge clots and worsen bleeding.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Pelvic trauma) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A client struck the head in a fall, lost consciousness briefly, then talked normally for 2 hours. The client now has a severe headache, vomiting, a dilated right pupil, and left arm weakness. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: A lumbar puncture to measure the intracranial pressure
options.B: Discharge instructions as the client was alert and talking normally for the past 2 hours
options.C: Oral analgesia and observation with checks every 4 hours
options.D: Emergency head CT and neurosurgical intervention for a possible epidural hematoma

correct: D) Emergency head CT and neurosurgical intervention for a possible epidural hematoma
rationale: A lucid interval followed by deterioration suggests an expanding epidural bleed that needs immediate imaging and surgery.
A: a puncture with a mass lesion risks herniation.
B: the alert period does not exclude a bleed.
C: slow observation delays treatment of an expanding mass.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Neurological (Head injury) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A construction worker has a traumatic forearm amputation with spurting bright red bleeding that is not controlled by direct pressure. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Apply a tourniquet 5 to 7 cm above the wound, tighten until the bleeding stops, and record the time
options.B: Place a loose tourniquet around the elbow and cover with a dressing
options.C: Elevate the arm and apply an ice pack to the stump
options.D: Apply a tourniquet directly over the wound and loosen it every 5 minutes

correct: A) Apply a tourniquet 5 to 7 cm above the wound, tighten until the bleeding stops, and record the time
rationale: Life-threatening limb bleeding uncontrolled by pressure needs a tourniquet above the wound, tightened until bleeding stops, with the time noted.
B: a loose tourniquet does not stop arterial bleeding.
C: elevation and ice do not control arterial bleeding.
D: placing it over the wound and loosening it repeatedly allows bleeding.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Hemorrhage control) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A worker has dry quicklime powder on the forearm and reports burning pain. Which action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Apply a neutralizing vinegar solution to the skin
options.B: Brush off the dry powder, remove contaminated clothing, and then flush with copious water
options.C: Cover the area with a dry dressing and transport the worker
options.D: Flush immediately with a high-pressure water stream

correct: B) Brush off the dry powder, remove contaminated clothing, and then flush with copious water
rationale: Dry chemical powder is brushed off first because water can activate it, and then the area is flushed.
A: neutralizing agents add heat and a second reaction.
C: covering without removal leaves the chemical in contact with the skin.
D: water on a large amount of powder can intensify the burn and spread the chemical.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Chemical burn) · Hard · Prioritization · Safety

stem: An 80-year-old client with three fractured ribs on the right reports severe pain with breathing and has an SpO2 of 91% with shallow respirations. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Bed rest flat with no deep breathing to protect the ribs
options.B: Opioid-free care to avoid respiratory depression
options.C: Tight binding of the chest to splint the ribs
options.D: Effective analgesia such as a regional block with incentive spirometry and close respiratory monitoring

correct: D) Effective analgesia such as a regional block with incentive spirometry and close respiratory monitoring
rationale: Pain-limited breathing leads to atelectasis and pneumonia in older adults, so strong analgesia with lung expansion measures is needed.
A: lying flat without deep breathing promotes atelectasis.
B: untreated pain causes shallow breathing and respiratory failure.
C: tight binding restricts breathing further.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Chest trauma) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Complication

stem: A client who received a drug-eluting coronary stent 6 weeks ago takes aspirin and clopidogrel and is scheduled tomorrow for an elective hernia repair. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Hold both antiplatelet drugs tonight and proceed with the surgery
options.B: Hold the aspirin and proceed with the surgery
options.C: Question proceeding with the elective surgery as stopping dual antiplatelet therapy early risks stent thrombosis
options.D: Give both drugs on the morning of surgery and proceed as scheduled

correct: C) Question proceeding with the elective surgery as stopping dual antiplatelet therapy early risks stent thrombosis
rationale: Stopping dual therapy within weeks of a stent risks thrombosis, so elective surgery is usually delayed.
A: stopping both leaves the stent unprotected.
B: stopping aspirin leaves only partial protection and still carries risk.
D: proceeding on both drugs raises surgical bleeding risk without addressing timing.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Perioperative (Antiplatelet therapy) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Safety

stem: A client received IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis from a bee sting, and the symptoms resolved within 20 minutes. The client asks to leave after 30 minutes of observation. Which response is best?

options.A: Observe for 30 more minutes and discharge if the vital signs are normal
options.B: Explain that symptoms can return hours later and that observation for several hours is recommended
options.C: Discharge with a prescription for an oral antihistamine and no epinephrine auto-injector device at home
options.D: Allow discharge as the symptoms resolved completely

correct: B) Explain that symptoms can return hours later and that observation for several hours is recommended
rationale: A biphasic reaction can occur hours after the first, so a longer observation period is advised.
A: an hour of observation is too short.
C: an antihistamine does not treat anaphylaxis and the client needs an epinephrine device.
D: resolution does not exclude a late return of symptoms.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Anaphylaxis) · Hard · Application · Safety

stem: A client with acute postoperative pain who has never taken opioids has a prescription for a fentanyl 50 mcg/hr transdermal patch. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Apply the patch and monitor sedation every 4 hours
options.B: Apply the patch and add a second patch for faster relief
options.C: Question the prescription as the patch is for opioid-tolerant clients with chronic pain
options.D: Apply the patch to a warm area to speed absorption

correct: C) Question the prescription as the patch is for opioid-tolerant clients with chronic pain
rationale: Fentanyl patches are for opioid-tolerant clients with stable chronic pain, and opioid-naive clients risk fatal respiratory depression.
A: monitoring does not make the dose safe in an opioid-naive client.
B: a second patch doubles a dangerous dose.
D: heat increases absorption and the risk of overdose.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Pharmacology in Medical-Surgical Care (Opioids) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Contraindication

stem: A client takes extended-release morphine 60 mg every 12 hours. The prescriber orders immediate-release morphine for breakthrough pain at 10% of the total daily dose. What dose should the nurse give?

options.A: 24 mg
options.B: 6 mg
options.C: 60 mg
options.D: 12 mg

correct: D) 12 mg
rationale: The total daily dose is 120 mg, and 10% is 12 mg.
A: this is 20% of the daily dose.
B: this is 10% of a single 60 mg dose.
C: this is a full extended-release dose.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Pharmacology in Medical-Surgical Care (Opioid dosing) · Hard · Application · Safety

stem: A client in a medical ICU has a prescription for an insulin infusion to keep the glucose between 80 and 110 mg/dL. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Titrate the infusion to the prescribed target without comment
options.B: Give a bolus of dextrose to prevent a glucose below 110 mg/dL
options.C: Question the target as current guidance supports 140 to 180 mg/dL to reduce hypoglycemia
options.D: Stop the infusion once the glucose reaches 150 mg/dL

correct: C) Question the target as current guidance supports 140 to 180 mg/dL to reduce hypoglycemia
rationale: Tight control in critically ill clients increases severe hypoglycemia and mortality, so a moderate target is recommended.
A: tight targets raise the risk of dangerous lows.
B: giving dextrose to a client on insulin at target defeats the purpose.
D: stopping at 150 without a plan risks uncontrolled hyperglycemia.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Endocrine (Inpatient glycemic control) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Safety

stem: Which client should receive sequential compression devices in place of pharmacologic prophylaxis for deep vein thrombosis?

options.A: Client with an active gastrointestinal bleed and a falling hemoglobin
options.B: Client with heart failure and a normal INR on admission
options.C: Client 2 days after hip replacement with a stable hemoglobin and platelets
options.D: Client on bed rest with pneumonia and normal platelets

correct: A) Client with an active gastrointestinal bleed and a falling hemoglobin
rationale: Active bleeding is a contraindication to anticoagulant prophylaxis, so mechanical devices are used.
B: heart failure with a normal INR supports drug prophylaxis.
C: stable postoperative clients are candidates for drug prophylaxis.
D: normal platelets and bed rest support drug prophylaxis.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Hematology (Thromboprophylaxis) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Contraindication

stem: A client after a bicycle collision has left upper quadrant pain, left shoulder pain, heart rate 122, blood pressure 88/54, and a distended tender abdomen. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: A laxative for the abdominal distention
options.B: A heating pad for the shoulder pain
options.C: Oral analgesia and a repeat examination in 24 hours
options.D: Immediate resuscitation with blood products and preparation for emergency surgery

correct: D) Immediate resuscitation with blood products and preparation for emergency surgery
rationale: Left upper quadrant and referred shoulder pain with shock suggest splenic rupture, which needs resuscitation and surgery.
A: a laxative does not address bleeding and risks harm.
B: heat treats a symptom and ignores the shock.
C: waiting 24 hours risks fatal hemorrhage.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Emergency (Abdominal trauma) · Hard · Prioritization · Emergency

stem: A client receives radioactive iodine for hyperthyroidism and will go home today. Which instruction should the nurse give?

options.A: Share the bed with the spouse and children as no precautions are needed
options.B: Avoid close contact with pregnant women and children for the days specified and flush the toilet twice
options.C: Use the same bathroom as others and wash hands once a day
options.D: Stay in a hospital isolation room for 4 weeks

correct: B) Avoid close contact with pregnant women and children for the days specified and flush the toilet twice
rationale: Radioactive iodine is excreted in body fluids, so limiting close contact and good hygiene protect others, especially children and pregnant women.
A: close contact exposes others to radiation.
C: shared bathrooms and infrequent hand washing spread contamination.
D: weeks of hospital isolation are unnecessary.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Endocrine (Radioactive iodine safety) · Hard · Application · Teaching

stem: A client in septic shock with a blood pressure of 70/40 and cold, mottled hands has a fingerstick glucose of 258 mg/dL. The last venous laboratory glucose was 112 mg/dL one hour ago. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Hold insulin and fluids until the next scheduled glucose check
options.B: Repeat the fingerstick on the same finger and treat if again elevated
options.C: Confirm with a venous or arterial blood sample as fingerstick results are unreliable with poor perfusion
options.D: Give a correction dose of insulin based on the fingerstick value

correct: C) Confirm with a venous or arterial blood sample as fingerstick results are unreliable with poor perfusion
rationale: Poor peripheral perfusion makes capillary glucose unreliable, so a laboratory sample guides therapy.
A: withholding fluids in shock is unsafe.
B: a repeat on the same cold finger repeats the error.
D: insulin based on an unreliable value risks hypoglycemia.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Endocrine (Point-of-care testing) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Safety

stem: A client with darker skin pigmentation has an SpO2 of 94% on the finger probe but appears pale, has a respiratory rate of 30, and is confused. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Document normal oxygenation as the saturation is above 92%
options.B: Obtain an arterial blood gas as pulse oximetry can overestimate saturation in darker skin
options.C: Reduce the oxygen to keep the saturation at 94%
options.D: Move the probe to the earlobe and accept the new value without any further clinical assessment

correct: B) Obtain an arterial blood gas as pulse oximetry can overestimate saturation in darker skin
rationale: Pulse oximeters can overestimate arterial saturation in darker skin, so the clinical picture and a blood gas guide care.
A: the client shows signs of respiratory distress despite the number.
C: reducing oxygen in a distressed client is unsafe.
D: a different site does not remove the measurement bias.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Respiratory (Oxygen monitoring) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Assessment

stem: A client is receiving vancomycin 1,250 mg IV every 12 hours, and a trough level is prescribed. When should the nurse draw the sample?

options.A: Immediately after the fourth dose finishes infusing
options.B: Midway between the third and fourth doses
options.C: Within 30 minutes before the fourth dose
options.D: Two hours after the first dose starts

correct: C) Within 30 minutes before the fourth dose
rationale: A trough reflects the lowest level at steady state, so it is drawn just before the fourth dose.
A: a sample after the infusion shows the peak.
B: a midpoint sample is neither trough nor peak.
D: an early sample does not show steady state.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Pharmacology in Medical-Surgical Care (Therapeutic drug monitoring) · Hard · Application · Monitoring

stem: Which electrolyte replacement prescription should the nurse question?

options.A: Potassium chloride 10 mEq/hr by infusion pump through a central line
options.B: Potassium chloride 20 mEq by IV push now for a potassium of 2.9 mEq/L
options.C: Potassium chloride 40 mEq in 1 L of 0.9% sodium chloride over 8 hours
options.D: Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 1 hour for a magnesium of 1.2 mg/dL

correct: B) Potassium chloride 20 mEq by IV push now for a potassium of 2.9 mEq/L
rationale: Direct IV push potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrest, and it is given only by controlled infusion.
A: controlled infusion at this rate is acceptable.
C: dilute infusion over 8 hours is acceptable.
D: slow magnesium replacement is acceptable.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Pharmacology in Medical-Surgical Care (High-alert medications) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Contraindication

stem: A client 1 hour after a right subclavian central line insertion has sudden dyspnea, a respiratory rate of 30, SpO2 of 88%, and absent breath sounds on the right. Blood pressure is 96/60. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Use of the new line for IV fluids while waiting for the morning chest x-ray
options.B: Removal of the line and application of a pressure dressing to the neck
options.C: Oxygen, an urgent chest x-ray, and preparation for chest tube insertion
options.D: A nebulized bronchodilator and reassessment in 1 hour

correct: C) Oxygen, an urgent chest x-ray, and preparation for chest tube insertion
rationale: Sudden hypoxemia with absent breath sounds after subclavian insertion suggests pneumothorax, which needs urgent imaging and drainage.
A: using an unconfirmed line and waiting until morning is unsafe.
B: removing the line does not treat the collapsed lung.
D: bronchodilators do not treat a pneumothorax.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Respiratory (Procedure complication) · Hard · Prioritization · Complication

stem: A client with kidney failure (eGFR 20) has a high clinical suspicion for pulmonary embolism and a normal chest x-ray. Which imaging study should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: A chest x-ray repeated as the definitive test
options.B: A contrast CT pulmonary angiogram with no kidney precautions
options.C: A D-dimer as the sole test to exclude the diagnosis
options.D: A ventilation-perfusion scan to avoid iodinated contrast

correct: D) A ventilation-perfusion scan to avoid iodinated contrast
rationale: In advanced kidney disease with a normal chest x-ray, a V/Q scan avoids contrast exposure.
A: a chest x-ray cannot confirm or exclude embolism.
B: contrast without precautions risks kidney injury.
C: a D-dimer does not exclude embolism when the suspicion is high.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Respiratory (Pulmonary embolism diagnosis) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Safety

stem: A client taking lisinopril and spironolactone is started on trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary infection. Five days later the potassium is 6.2 mEq/L and the ECG shows peaked T waves. Which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate as the sole treatment
options.B: Calcium gluconate, holding the offending drugs, and treatment to shift and remove potassium
options.C: Continuation of all three drugs with a repeat potassium in a week
options.D: A potassium-rich diet to support the heart

correct: B) Calcium gluconate, holding the offending drugs, and treatment to shift and remove potassium
rationale: Three potassium-raising drugs together cause hyperkalemia, and ECG changes need membrane protection and removal of the cause.
A: a binder is too slow for ECG changes.
C: continuing the drugs worsens the hyperkalemia.
D: added potassium is dangerous.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Fluids and Electrolytes (Drug-induced hyperkalemia) · Hard · Clinical Judgment · Adverse Effect

stem: A client takes digoxin 0.25 mg daily at 0900, and the prescriber orders a serum digoxin level. When should the nurse draw the blood to obtain an accurate result?

options.A: Immediately after the 0900 dose is given
options.B: Two hours after the dose when the drug is at its peak effect in the heart
options.C: One hour after the dose at peak absorption
options.D: At least 6 to 8 hours after the dose or just before the next dose

correct: D) At least 6 to 8 hours after the dose or just before the next dose
rationale: Digoxin takes hours to distribute to tissues, so earlier samples overestimate the level.
A: a sample right after the dose reflects the dose, not the steady level.
B: a 2-hour sample is still in the distribution phase.
C: peak absorption misrepresents tissue levels.
tag: Medical-Surgical Nursing · Pharmacology in Medical-Surgical Care (Therapeutic drug monitoring) · Hard · Application · Monitoring
